rows.name: cna_color_copy_debug_string
rows.reason: XNA's math, geometry, curve, colour and packed-value semantics are deterministic and are implemented exactly in TypeScript; the differential corpus pins them against the reference implementation. Calling native to *evaluate* them would add a handle, an error path and a backend dependency to operations XNA performs with no failure mode at all. Note that purpose is not reachability: thirteen of these routes are reached, because `cna_cnb_decode_curve` hands back a native curve and the only way to lift it into the managed one is to read its loop modes and its keys. The native object is released inside that call and the curve a consumer holds still evaluates in TypeScript.

rows.name: cna_half_from_single
rows.reason: XNA's math, geometry, curve, colour and packed-value semantics are deterministic and are implemented exactly in TypeScript; the differential corpus pins them against the reference implementation. Calling native to *evaluate* them would add a handle, an error path and a backend dependency to operations XNA performs with no failure mode at all. Note that purpose is not reachability: thirteen of these routes are reached, because `cna_cnb_decode_curve` hands back a native curve and the only way to lift it into the managed one is to read its loop modes and its keys. The native object is released inside that call and the curve a consumer holds still evaluates in TypeScript.

rows.name: cna_math_barycentric
rows.reason: XNA's math, geometry, curve, colour and packed-value semantics are deterministic and are implemented exactly in TypeScript; the differential corpus pins them against the reference implementation. Calling native to *evaluate* them would add a handle, an error path and a backend dependency to operations XNA performs with no failure mode at all. Note that purpose is not reachability: thirteen of these routes are reached, because `cna_cnb_decode_curve` hands back a native curve and the only way to lift it into the managed one is to read its loop modes and its keys. The native object is released inside that call and the curve a consumer holds still evaluates in TypeScript.
